title: LTSV: Layered Type-Constrained Shapley Value for Heterogeneous Graph Data Valuation

problem.claim: Data valuation is needed to quantify data worth and attribute contributions fairly in multi-party machine-learning collaborations.

gap.claim: Existing Shapley-value methods for IID data do not readily extend to heterogeneous graphs because of type-dependent roles, cross-type dependencies, and high valuation costs.

contributions.claim: LTSV decomposes each node's value into intra-type feature contribution, cross-type semantic bridging, and global structural support.
LTSV uses type-constrained subgames to support axiomatic fairness for within-type contributions while retaining heterogeneous context.
LTSV makes unlabeled bridge-node contributions explicit through meta-path-based propagation and scales valuation with type-constrained Monte Carlo sampling and importance weighting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On DBLP, ACM, and IMDb, LTSV reportedly identifies high-value nodes more accurately than state-of-the-art baselines under standard deletion/addition evaluations.
The authors report favorable computational efficiency on DBLP, ACM, and IMDb.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data valuation supports fair contribution attribution in multi-party machine learning.
Heterogeneous graphs introduce type-dependent roles, cross-type dependencies, and costly valuation that challenge existing Shapley methods.
LTSV decomposes node value, anchors valuation in type-constrained subgames, and propagates value through meta-paths.
Type-constrained Monte Carlo sampling with importance weighting is used to scale valuation.
Experiments on three datasets report improved node identification accuracy and favorable computational efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The method separates node value into within-type, cross-type, and global structural components.

interpretation.claim: Decomposing heterogeneous contributions by relational role may make valuation more interpretable.

application.claim: Use role- or type-specific value components when designing valuation methods for multi-relational data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the decomposition is appropriate for domains without meaningful node types or structural roles.

source_observation.claim: The method uses importance-weighted Monte Carlo sampling to reduce valuation cost.

interpretation.claim: Structured sampling may improve the scalability of expensive cooperative-value estimates.

application.claim: Consider constrained or importance-weighted sampling when exact valuation is computationally prohibitive.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify sampling error, weighting assumptions, or conditions under which efficiency gains hold.

unknowns: No quantitative accuracy or efficiency results are provided.
No details are given about datasets, baselines, evaluation protocols, sampling error, or computational resources.
No full-text information is available about theoretical guarantees beyond the stated fairness anchoring.
